dedupe_keys.name: wind tunnel loads on the wind excited benchmark high rise building nees 2014 1241 along wind and across wind

description: These two NEES datasets hold the wind tunnel measurements behind the wind-excited benchmark building, a 76-storey high-rise used across structural control research to compare damping and control strategies under wind. They were deposited by Bijan Samali in 2014 with the Network for Earthquake Engineering Simulation, and are now served from the DesignSafe-CI Data Depot as project NEES-2014-1241, Experiment 1 (along-wind) and Experiment 2 (across-wind). Each experiment gives one hour (3,600 seconds) of fluctuating wind forces including the mean load, derived by similitude from pressures recorded on the small-scale model, as 32 Excel files of forces on each panel apportioned to floor levels, plus pressure coefficients; the original paper is in the documentation folder. Access: open download from DesignSafe with DataCite DOIs 10.4231/d32n4zj6g and 10.4231/d3xw47x1g. Licence: the DataCite records carry no licence statement; free. Caveats: one building shape and one wind climate, scaled from a wind tunnel, so the loads are a benchmark, not a site record. Simulation uses are validation of wind-load and structural response models and tests of control and resilience measures for tall buildings. Related records: the AIJ urban wind environment benchmark datasets.
